whatItIs.text: Soy milk coagulated and pressed into blocks — silken through extra-firm — with over 2,000 years of history and one of the lowest land and carbon footprints of any protein source.

historyNote.text: Tofu-making was first recorded in China's Han dynasty, and legend credits Prince Liu An (179-122 BC) with the invention; it reached Japan during the Nara period (710-794), and the English word appeared in 1704 in a translation of Navarrete's voyages.

howToChoose.text: Match firmness to job: silken for dressings and desserts, firm or extra-firm for frying and scrambling; vacuum packs should look clean and smell faintly sweet, never sour.

storage.text: Once opened, cover with fresh water in a container and refrigerate, changing the water daily.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Extra-firm tofu becomes chewy roasted bites; frozen tofu turns sponge-like and soaks up sauce; silken tofu thickens smoothies and soups.
